items.question: Are these EnviroMET prices?
items.answer: No. Enter your own estimates or supplier quotations. The calculator does not assume equipment prices, financing terms or a guaranteed saving.

items.question: What does the comparison include?
items.answer: For each site: initial setup plus campaign months multiplied by monthly operating costs, plus planned visits multiplied by cost per visit. Totals are multiplied by the number of sites.

items.question: How are ROI and payback calculated?
items.answer: If Option B has higher initial setup costs and lower monthly operating costs, simple ROI equals net campaign savings divided by additional setup investment. Payback divides that investment by monthly operating savings. Visit costs are included in total savings but excluded from monthly payback because their timing is unspecified.

items.text: EnviroMET technical editorial · Published 10 October 2026 · Planning guidance

A solar campaign should distinguish resource characterisation from operating-plant monitoring. Define the required irradiance quantities, meteorological observations, instrument locations and recording intervals with the assessment team. The selected sensors and station configuration should serve those requirements.
items.blockName: A solar campaign should distinguish resource characterisatio…

items.text: Station siting, horizon obstruction, levelling, alignment where applicable, cleanliness and maintenance records affect interpretation. In a remote setting, access for inspection and instrument care should be planned together with the power and communications system. Agree which activities are performed remotely and which require a field visit.
items.blockName: Station siting, horizon obstruction, levelling, alignment wh…

items.text: Retain instrument identification, calibration information, station configuration and any changes made during the campaign. Review time-series data for gaps and unusual behaviour. Where several observation sources are used, document how site measurements relate to other resource inputs instead of treating them as interchangeable.
items.blockName: Retain instrument identification, calibration information, s…

items.text: Agree the expected data format, QA/QC outputs, service records and interpretation scope. Resource and energy-yield assessment also depend on modelling assumptions beyond the station itself. The campaign should provide clear observations and records so those assumptions can be reviewed.
items.blockName: Agree the expected data format, QA/QC outputs, service recor…

items.text: EnviroMET supports solar-station configuration, instrumentation, installation, maintenance and resource assessment. items.label: Bring the right information to the first discussion
items.blockName: Bring the right information to the first discussion

items.text: A wind-resource campaign should answer a defined project question: early site screening, a resource assessment, a turbine-performance campaign or an operating-site review. The objective changes the required locations, measurement heights, instrumentation, records and reporting. A mast or LiDAR specification is a consequence of that objective, rather than the starting point.
items.blockName: A wind-resource campaign should answer a defined project que…

items.text: Met masts provide observations at the installed sensor positions. Ground-mounted LiDAR provides remote observations at configured heights. Site conditions, terrain, access, power availability, verification arrangements and assessment requirements all affect selection. A combined approach may be appropriate where it resolves an identified measurement or verification need; it is not automatically the best choice for every site.
items.blockName: Met masts provide observations at the installed sensor posit…

items.text: Instrument configuration, mounting, calibration records, data logger settings, power and communications form one measurement chain. Define how time stamps, configuration changes, outages, field visits and maintenance will be recorded. A reliable campaign also needs a practical plan for spare equipment, access and escalation when remote monitoring identifies an issue.
items.blockName: Instrument configuration, mounting, calibration records, dat…

items.text: The scope should establish applicable measurement standards, verification requirements, data checks and the reporting audience. IEC 61400-50-1 concerns mast-mounted measurements; IEC 61400-50-2 concerns ground-mounted vertical-profiling remote sensing. The assessor determines what evidence is needed for the intended assessment. Neither an equipment name nor a reference to a standard guarantees acceptance for financing.

items.text: Share coordinates, site boundaries, available access information, project stage, target measurement heights and the decision the data will support. If a resource assessor or lender has already specified campaign requirements, include them. EnviroMET can then discuss planning, met mast or LiDAR delivery, system integration, maintenance and data review around that scope.

items.question: How long should a wind campaign run?
items.answer: The required period depends on the assessment objective, seasonal coverage and stakeholder requirements. Agree duration and data-quality expectations with the project assessor rather than treating one fixed period as suitable for every site.
items.blockName: How long should a wind campaign run?

items.question: What makes wind data bankable?
items.answer: Bankability depends on the suitability, traceability, uncertainty treatment and completeness of the measurement and assessment, together with acceptance by the relevant stakeholders. A sensor or logger alone cannot establish it.
